author: nickheyer
body:
Modules are managed sidecar services/container scoped to a minecraft server instance. They have access to the same network and therefore the minecraft server itself. They can be configured dynamically based on any configuration value present in the context of that server. Modules can optionally "track" the lifetime of the parent minecraft server, syncing with it's start ups and shutdowns. 

Module templates are the "blueprint" for a module's creation. There are two types: built-in (ships with discopanel) and custom (you design your own service, kind of like a docker compose, but with access to everything you'd ever need inside discopanel). You can theoretically run anything as a Module, as long as it runs inside of a docker container, which is why Module templates require a docker image to pull/run. 

Two "Protocols" introduced. Raw TCP forwarding (hostname path based proxying not applicable here, requires a proxy route to listen at a unique tcp port on the host). Moved the Minecraft protocol (and officially titled it as such) to it's own protocol choice for a route. Added UDP forwarding, similar to TCP it can not on its own use hostname / path based proxying only a IP:PORT (which still works from dns), so a UDP port needs to be listened on / bound to proxy - this was added for geyser/bedrock support. Finally, HTTP is the last protocol added - this (and minecraft too) are technically not "protocols" like TCP/UDP, but rather an abstraction of it - nonetheless this works much like a typical http reverse proxy for modules, etc. Allowing you to host any arbitrary web server or web app on the same proxied hostname as your minecraft server!

author: copilot
body:
Moving parallelization from scanline to triangle level introduced race conditions where multiple threads simultaneously wrote to overlapping pixels, corrupting z-buffer depth tests and causing visual artifacts.

## Changes

**Moved parallelization from triangle loop to scanline pixel loop**
- Removed `#pragma omp parallel for` from `device_render()` triangle iteration (line 964)
- Added `#pragma omp parallel for if((ex - sx) > 64)` to `device_processScanLine()` pixel loop (line 798)
- Each thread now processes distinct X coordinates within a scanline—no pixel conflicts possible

**Key insight**: Sequential triangle processing + parallel pixel processing = zero contention without atomics.

```c
// Before: Multiple threads render overlapping triangles → race on shared pixels
#pragma omp parallel for
for(indexVertices = 0; indexVertices < faceCount; indexVertices++) {
    device_drawTriangle(...);  // Thread A and B both write pixel(100,200)
}

// After: One scanline at a time, threads handle different X coordinates
for(indexVertices = 0; indexVertices < faceCount; indexVertices++) {
    device_drawTriangle(...) {
        #pragma omp parallel for if((ex - sx) > 64)
        for (x = sx; x < ex; x++) {  // Thread A: x=0-63, Thread B: x=64-127
            device_drawPoint(...);    // Disjoint pixels = no races
        }
    }
}
```

**Threshold optimization**: Only parallelize scanlines >64 pixels to avoid threading overhead on short spans.

## Documentation

- `PARALLEL_RENDERING_FIX.md`: Technical explanation and performance analysis
- `IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY_PARALLEL_FIX.md`: Implementation overview

body:
## Summary

Moves the inlet position from `[0, 0, 0.0]` to `[0, 0, 0.5]` in the malaria_venule_bifurcating_tree example spec to fix port connectivity issues.

The port carving algorithm carves in the OPPOSITE direction of the port's `direction` field. With the inlet at z=0.0 and direction `[0, 0, -1]`, the carving went upward while the void (tree) grew downward, causing the port to not connect to the void space.

By moving the inlet to z=0.5mm:
- The inlet sphere (radius 0.5mm) extends from z=0.0mm to z=1.0mm, touching the top surface
- The port carving goes upward from z=0.5mm and overlaps with the inlet sphere
- The tree grows downward from z=0.5mm into the domain
- This should connect the port to the void and eliminate the disconnected component

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

author: qf-jonathan
body:
### SUMMARY
Fixes a critical bug where editing roles with many users fails due to URL length limits, plus a secondary N+1 query optimization.

#### 1. Fix "Request Line is too large" error when editing roles with many users (Primary)
**Problem:** When editing a role with hundreds/thousands of users, the request to `/api/v1/security/users/?q=(filters:!((col:id,opr:in,value:!($USER_IDs)))...)` would fail because the URL became too long. This caused the user list to fail loading, and saving changes would inadvertently remove all role memberships.

**Solution:** Changed from filtering by user IDs (`col: 'id', opr: 'in', value: user_ids`) to filtering by role relationship (`col: 'roles', opr: 'rel_m_m', value: role_id`). The URL length now remains constant regardless of the number of users.

#### 2. Fix N+1 query issue in `/api/v1/security/roles/` endpoint (Secondary)
Also I noticed that the Changed SQLAlchemy loading strategy from `joinedload` to `selectinload` for `Role.permissions`, `Role.user`, and `Role.groups`. This eliminates N+1 queries when accessing `[user.id for user in role.user]`, `[perm.id for perm in role.permissions]`, and `[group.id for group in role.groups]` for each role.

Added a test to verify the correct filter parameters are sent to the API.

### BEFORE/AFTER SCREENSHOTS OR ANIMATED GIF

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b598fc0b-4ef7-4829-ae43-319c16f7a29f



### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS
1. Create a role with 2000+ users assigned
2. Navigate to Settings > Security > List Roles and click edit on that role
3. Verify the modal opens and displays users (previously would fail with "Request Line is too large")
4. Make a change and save
5. Verify all users remain assigned (previously would remove all memberships)
6. Check network tab - `/api/v1/security/users/` should use `rel_m_m` filter with short URL

Implements a visual particle simulation demonstrating electromagnetic interactions with a dedicated UI panel displaying mathematical formulas and live calculations.

## Implementation

**Core Physics Engine**
- Coulomb's Law for electrostatic forces between charged particles
- Newton's equations of motion (F=ma, velocity/position integration)
- Elastic boundary collisions with energy damping

author: songka
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent wheel sectors from being removed before a winner announcement finishes by reliably coordinating TTS playback completion.  
- Ensure automatic consecutive draws (`auto_wait` / auto-draw) continue until a prize's remaining slots are filled and remove the intermittent missed TTS playback.  
- Make the draw/removal/summary flow deterministic so announcements always finish before removal and the queue is refilled when needed.

### Description
- Initialize shared TTS synchronization primitives in `__init__`: add `self.tts_done_event`, `self.tts_lock`, and a shared `self.tts_engine` (created when `TTS_AVAILABLE`).
- Rewrite `_speak_winner` to clear `tts_done_event` at start, run the engine under `with self.tts_lock` in a background thread, and always set `tts_done_event` in `finally` (also toggles `self.tts_playing`).
- Gate the announcing phase on the event by changing the animator check to use `if self.tts_done_event.is_set():` and only then call `_begin_removal_after_announcement()`.
- Change `_handle_stop` to defer removal: populate `pending_removal_data`/`pending_removal_idx`, call `_speak_winner`, determine `self.post_removal_phase` based on current prize `remaining_slots` and `target_queue` (`prize_summary` when done, otherwise `auto_wait`), and set `phase = 'announcing'` (so removal happens only after TTS).
- Implement/adjust removal completion flow: add `_begin_removal_after_announcement`, `_complete_post_removal_phase`, and `_finalize_removal` so actual wheel removal happens after announcement and post-removal behavior refills the draw queue when `post_removal_phase == 'auto_wait'` and there are still slots to fill.
- Make wheel preparation and draw logic respect prize-specific exclusion (`exclude_previous_winners`) when building `clean_excluded_ids` and when pre-filling the `target_queue` via `_start_draw_logic` so auto-draw will generate the full set of winners for the current prize.
- Minor UX/UI updates: added `announcing` phase handling in `_update_btn_state` and other small visual/theme adjustments (red/gold palette) to align the UI with the updated flow.

### Testing
- Automated tests: none were executed for this change.

author: kvanhimbergen
body:
### Motivation
- Provide mandatory, machine-readable provenance for all backtest/sweep/walk-forward outputs so every run is reproducible and auditable.
- Ensure `run_id` is deterministic and derived only from stable inputs (`git_sha`, `config_hash`, `data_hash`, `execution_mode`, `parameters_used`) and not runtime metadata.
- Fail loudly when required provenance fields would be omitted or invalid to prevent partial artifacts.

### Description
- Add a new shared helper module `provenance.py` that implements canonical JSON serialization, `compute_data_hash`, `compute_config_hash`, `compute_run_id`, `git_sha` retrieval, `validate_execution_mode`, and `require_provenance_fields` enforcement.
- Embed provenance into single backtests by extending `run_backtest` to compute `run_id`, `git_sha`, `config_hash`, `data_hash`, `data_path`, `execution_mode`, and `parameters_used`, and to write `run_meta.json` and include provenance in `summary.json`, using `require_provenance_fields` to validate before writing.
- Wire provenance into sweep and walk-forward runs in `backtest_sweep.py` by computing `execution_mode`, computing per-run `run_id` using canonicalized parameters, writing per-run `run_meta.json` with `execution_mode` and `parameters_used`, and validating provenance presence.
- Extend parity checks in `parity.py` to include provenance fields (including `run_id` where reasonable) in `backtests/parity/parity_report.json` and validate required provenance fields; preserve parity diff behavior (report always written, diff written only on mismatch).
- Add tests: `tests/test_provenance.py` validates provenance fields in `summary.json` and `run_meta.json`, `run_id` stability and drift rules, and parity report provenance; update `tests/test_sweep_runner.py` to use the new `compute_run_id` signature and register the new test in `tests/run_tests.py`.

### Testing
- Added automated tests `tests/test_provenance.py` and updated `tests/test_sweep_runner.py`, and registered them to run via the existing wrapper `python tests/run_tests.py`.
- Ran `python tests/run_tests.py`; the test run aborted during collection with `ModuleNotFoundError` due to missing environment packages (`numpy`/`pandas`) in the execution environment, so the new tests were not executed to completion.
- Unit tests themselves assert the required provenance fields, `run_id` determinism and drift, and parity report provenance; they should pass deterministically once the environment has the required dependencies installed and `python tests/run_tests.py` is re-run.

body:
## Summary

Adds a comprehensive `/upgrade-dep` skill that provides a repeatable workflow for reviewing dependency upgrade PRs.

## Motivation

We frequently handle dependency upgrade PRs (like #7107) that require careful analysis of:
- Breaking changes and their impact on our codebase
- New features we can adopt
- Comprehensive testing to ensure stability
- CI verification before approval

This skill automates and standardizes that review process while ensuring thoroughness.

## What the Skill Does

The `/upgrade-dep <PR_URL>` command guides through an 8-step review workflow:

1. **Fetch PR Context** - Extracts dependency info and checks CI status immediately
2. **Gather Release Information** - Fetches changelogs and release notes
3. **Analyze Our Usage** - Greps codebase to understand how we use the dependency
4. **Impact Analysis** - Cross-references breaking changes with our usage
5. **Create Test Plan** - Generates specific tests based on usage locations
6. **Execute Tests** - Runs unit, integration, build, and linting tests
7. **Verify CI Status (CRITICAL)** - Ensures all CI checks pass before recommending approval
8. **Generate Summary** - Creates comprehensive review with enhancement proposals

## Key Features

- **Never auto-posts to PRs** - Always asks user permission first
- **Proactive enhancement proposals** - Suggests new features to build with:
  - Implementation strategies and file references
  - TypeScript type definitions for new config properties
  - YAML configuration examples
  - Complexity estimates and backward compatibility analysis
- **CI verification is mandatory** - Will not recommend APPROVE with failing CI
- **Comprehensive testing** - Validates changes with unit, integration, and build tests
- **Structured output** - Consistent review format for easy consumption

## Example Usage

```bash
/upgrade-dep https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/pull/7107
```

The skill will analyze the PR, test locally, check CI, propose enhancements, and present findings for user approval before posting.

## Testing

Tested on PR #7107 (@openai/codex-sdk upgrade) - see review comment there for example output.

author: kalenikaliaksandr
body:
This fixes a regression introduced in bf77aeb3dc029b2b4633463a5984cdaa439d0e8a which added support for WPT variant meta tags.

The problem occurs when a text test has no corresponding expectation file. The test should fail, but instead it passes. This happens because of the following execution flow:

1. Test loads and on_load_finish is called
2. internals.loadTestVariants() is executed (for all text tests)
3. The test JS calls signalTestIsDone(), setting did_finish_test = true
4. The variant metadata callback fires with an empty array (no variants)
5. In on_test_variant_metadata, since did_finish_test is true, it directly calls view.on_test_complete({ test_index, TestResult::Pass })

The bug is in step 5: the code bypasses handle_completed_test() which is where the expectation file comparison happens. Instead of calling on_test_complete() (the lambda that invokes handle_completed_test), it directly returns Pass.

The fix captures on_test_complete in the on_test_variant_metadata lambda and calls it instead of directly returning Pass, ensuring that the expectation file check is performed.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent confusing low-level errors caused by reading the error response body twice (e.g. “body stream already read”) when the server returns plain text/HTML instead of JSON. 
- Ensure users see clear, actionable messages when the submission edge function is offline, blocked, or rate-limited (`404`, `401/403`, `429`).
- Avoid wasted requests triggered by hidden autofill/honeypot fields and fail fast on the client when those are populated.

### Description
- Updated `callboard.html` to read the response body once via `response.text()` and attempt `JSON.parse` on that text instead of calling `response.json()` first.  
- Preserved and mapped status-specific messages for `404`, `401/403`, and `429`, and used parsed `message` fields when available.  
- Added an early client-side honeypot check that blocks submissions when the hidden `companyWebsite` field is populated and surfaces a clear autofill/spam warning.  
- Logged response status and parsed/trimmed error details via `console.error`, and surfaced thrown `Error` messages to `setFormStatus` (uses `error.message`).  
- Added a `CHANGELOG_RUNNING.md` entry documenting the change and verification checklist.

author: koteev-m
body:
### Motivation

- Add data-driven hall plan support so admins can upload PNG/JPEG floor plans and guests (and admin previews) can retrieve them as bytes with correct caching semantics and without breaking existing booking/layout ETag logic.

### Description

- Create a persistent `hall_plans` table and Flyway migrations (`V026__hall_plans.sql`) to store plan bytes, content type, sha256, size and timestamps.
- Add `HallPlan` model and `HallPlansRepository` interface in `core-domain`, and implement it in `LayoutDbRepository` with a transactional upsert that also atomically bumps `halls.layout_revision` and `halls.updated_at` to ensure layout ETag/watermark changes when plan changes (`upsertPlan` / `getPlanForClub`).
- Add Ktor routes: admin upload `PUT /api/admin/halls/{hallId}/plan` (multipart, file field `file`, allows `image/png` and `image/jpeg`, rejects SVG, enforces 5MB limit, returns metadata JSON) and guest retrieval `GET /api/clubs/{clubId}/halls/{hallId}/plan` (raw bytes, preserved `Content-Type`, strong ETag `plan-sha256-<hex>`, supports `If-None-Match`→`304`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, must-revalidate`, and `Vary: X-Telegram-Init-Data`).
- Wire DI: expose `HallPlansRepository` from the base `LayoutRepository` in `LayoutModule`, and register the new route modules in `Application.module()`.
- Add tests `HallPlanRoutesTest` (Ktor `testApplication`) that cover rejecting SVG/wrong content type, rejecting oversized payloads, successful upload → fetch bytes + Content-Type + ETag, 304 on `If-None-Match`, and verify layout ETag lastUpdatedAt is bumped after upload.

### Testing

- No automated test suite was executed in this rollout; new Ktor tests were added at `app-bot/src/test/kotlin/com/example/bot/routes/HallPlanRoutesTest.kt` and should be run locally or in CI.
- Run the full test matrix with `./gradlew test --console=plain --fail-fast` to validate the changes (expected: new tests exercise upload/retrieval/ETag behaviors).

body:
### Motivation

- Replace the existing small shape-matching puzzle with an 8×8 tango-style grid that mirrors the requested arc/spire aesthetic and gameplay constraints. 
- Provide fixed clue cells and pairwise equality/contrast clues so the puzzle plays like a typical "tango" logic puzzle.

### Description

- Reworked `app/games/shape-puzzle/ShapePuzzleGame.tsx` to implement an 8×8 grid using two shapes (`arc` and `spire`), with an internal `solutionGrid`, a set of `fixedCells`, and visual constraint markers rendered between adjacent cells. 
- Added rule validation and UI feedback for row/column balance (four of each shape per line), three-in-a-row detection, and constraint (same/different) violations, exposing per-line status and invalid-cell highlighting. 
- Updated interactions and copy: tiles cycle through `arc → spire → empty`, `Shift+click` advances two steps, move counter, selection panel, and finished/Reset UI.

### Testing

- Ran `pnpm build`, which reported failure to download Google Fonts in this environment and therefore could not complete font download (build environment fell back to local fonts); the font fetch issue is environmental and unrelated to the code changes.

body:
The issue requested documentation of how Overall Status and Form Analysis stats are determined and displayed on the processed video page. ## Documentation Added ### Japanese Documentation (`STATS_LOGIC_DOCUMENTATION.md`) Comprehensive 329-line reference covering: - **Overall Status**: `"EGO LIFT"` if hip lift OR shallow rep detected, else `"GOOD REP"` - **Hip Lift Detection**: Baseline hip-to-bench distance at start; violation when `current > baseline + (baseline × 0.5)` - **Shallow Rep Detection**: State machine tracking bar-shoulder distance; flags when elbow at lowest point exceeds `bench_top + (torso_length × 0.05)` - **Video Info**: FPS, total frames, duration extracted via OpenCV - Complete data flow from YOLO/MediaPipe analysis → JSON results → database polling (5s intervals, 10min max) → UI display - Configuration constants, debugging tips, file references with line numbers ### English Overview (`docs/STATS_LOGIC_OVERVIEW_EN.md`) 265-line quick reference with algorithm pseudocode, technology stack details (YOLO for bench/bar detection, MediaPipe for pose landmarks), and customization guide. ### Updated README Added Documentation section linking to all reference materials. ## Technical Details Detection algorithms run in `ml-backend/app/logic.py`: ```python # Hip Lift: Dynamic threshold based on initial position baseline_hip_bench_dist = abs(current_hip_y - bench_top_y) dynamic_hip_threshold = baseline_hip_bench_dist * HIP_LIFT_RATIO # 0.5 if current_hip_bench_dist > (baseline_hip_bench_dist + dynamic_hip_threshold): hip_lift_status = "FAIL: HIP LIFT" # Shallow Rep: State machine with torso-relative threshold dynamic_shallow_threshold = abs(shoulder_y - hip_y) * SHALLOW_REP_RATIO # 0.05 if is_in_rep and min_elbow_y_at_bottom > (bench_top_y + dynamic_shallow_threshold): shallow_rep_status = "FAIL: ELBOW DEPTH" ``` Results saved to JSON alongside processed video, polled by frontend at 5s intervals up to 10min timeout before marking FAILED.

openspec proposal which can be used to assist in implementing #133 

proposes a `palette.selector` feature to let site visitors choose theme palettes (ex: dark vs light, or a dropdown with more than 2 palette options)

example interface:

```yaml
theme:
  name: terminal
  palette:
    default: dark
    selector:
      enabled: true
      ui: auto   # values: auto | toggle | select
      options:
        - dark
        - light
        - solarized

the proposal also specifies that users should be able to include their own custom CSS as an option as long as they have included the css in `extra_css`

backwards compatibility is specified so that users who have their site configured to use `palette: dark` wil not be impacted

author: lan17
body:
# PR Description

## 🚀 Overview
This PR introduces the **V2 Class-Based Plugin Architecture** to standardise how all components (Sources, Filters, Analyzers, Notifiers) are registered, configured, and instantiated. It also includes significant stability improvements for **RTSP Sources**, addressing "zombie thread" issues and allowing robust configuration of FFmpeg.

## ✨ Key Changes

### 1. V2 Plugin Architecture
Refactored the entire plugin system from ad-hoc functional factories to a unified, type-safe class-based system.
-   **Unified Registry**: Single `PluginRegistry` handles all plugin types.
-   **`@plugin` Decorator**: Plugins declare their metadata (name, type) via a clean decorator.
-   **Configuration as Contract**: All plugins now define a Pydantic `config_cls`. Configuration is validated *before* plugin creation.
-   **Dependency Injection**: Standardized injection of runtime dependencies (like `camera_name` or `overrides`) into config models or factory methods, removing the need for complex "Context" objects.
-   **Refactored Components**:
    -   `LocalFolderSource`: Removed coupled dependency on `StateStore`. Now uses a clean `.homesec_state.json` manifest pattern.
    -   All Plugins (YOLO, OpenAI, MQTT, SendGrid, etc.) ported to V2.

### 2. RTSP Robustness & Stability
Addressed frequent reconnection loops and silent failures in RTSP streams.
-   **Fix "Zombie" Threads**: Fixed a bug in `ThreadedClipSource` where dead background threads reported as "Healthy". The system now correctly detects crashes and restarts the component (this was the cause of "instability" — it was actually improved observability of existing failures).
-   **Configurable FFmpeg Flags**: Added `ffmpeg_flags` list to `RTSPSourceConfig`. Users can now inject arbitrary flags (e.g., `-rtsp_transport udp`, buffer sizes) via YAML.
-   **Robust Defaults**:
    -   **Logging**: Changed default `ffmpeg` log level from quiet to `warning` to capture failure reasons.
    -   **Timestamp Fixes**: Added `-fflags +genpts+igndts` by default to handle cheap cameras with bad clocks (fixes "Non-monotonous DTS" errors).
    -   **Framerate**: Added `-fps_mode passthrough` to stop frame dropping on variable-rate streams.

### 3. Documentation & Cleanup
-   **`DESIGN.md`**: Updated to reflect the ground-truth V2 architecture. Removed "Proposed" sections and legacy file references (`src/human_filter` -> `src/homesec/plugins/filters...`).
-   **`PLUGIN_DEVELOPMENT.md`**: Added a new "Common Plugin Structure" guide to help developers build new V2 plugins.
-   **Cleanup**: Removed the obsolete `docs/decisions` directory (ADRs superseded by this refactor).

## 🧪 Verification
-   **Unit Tests**: Updated `test_plugin_registration.py` and `test_app.py` to verify the new registry and config injection.
-   **Integration**: Verified faulty RTSP streams now logs warnings to `recordings/frame_pipeline.log` instead of failing silently.
-   **Type Safety**: `mypy` check passes with strict typing on the new registry.

author: katamotokosuke
body:
## Summary

- AWS Role Chainingをサポートし、長時間実行ジョブでの自動認証情報リフレッシュを実現
- 静的なAWS認証情報（aws_access_key_id等）をAssumeRoleベースの認証に置き換え
- 認証情報の有効期限5分前に自動リフレッシュ

## Background

AWS Role Chainingを使用する場合、AWSの仕様により最大セッション時間が1時間に制限されます。従来の実装では静的なAWS認証情報を設定で受け取っていたため、プラグイン内部でのリフレッシュができず、1時間以上のジョブで認証情報が期限切れになる問題がありました。

## Changes

| ファイル | 変更内容 |
|---------|---------|
| `AwsRoleCredentialsSupplier.java` | **新規** - AssumeRole + 自動リフレッシュ |
| `WorkloadIdentityFederationConfig.java` | 設定項目を変更 |
| `WorkloadIdentityFederationAuth.java` | Supplierパターンに変更 |
| `WorkloadIdentityFederationCredentials.java` | CacheKey変更 |
| `shadow-google-cloud-bigquery-helper/build.gradle` | AWS SDK STS依存関係を追加 |
| `AwsRoleCredentialsSupplierTest.java` | **新規** |
| `WorkloadIdentityFederationAuthTest.java` | **新規** |

## Breaking Changes

設定スキーマが変更されます：

```yaml
# Before
workload_identity_federation:
  config: /path/to/wif-config.json
  aws_access_key_id: AKIAXXXXXXXXXX
  aws_secret_access_key: xxxxxxxxxxxxx
  aws_session_token: xxxxx
  aws_region: ap-northeast-1

# After
workload_identity_federation:
  config: /path/to/wif-config.json
  aws_role_arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/role-name
  aws_role_session_name: embulk-bigquery-output  # optional, default: "embulk-bigquery-output"
  aws_region: ap-northeast-1                      # optional, default: "ap-northeast-1"
```

## Test plan

- [x] ユニットテスト実行 (`./gradlew test`)
- [ ] EKS環境での統合テスト（IRSA使用）

⏱️ Runtime : **`119 milliseconds`** **→** **`2.48 milliseconds`** (best of `37` runs)

#### 📝 Explanation and details


The optimized code achieves a **4706% speedup** (119ms → 2.48ms) by introducing **memoization** for the expensive `detect_langs()` call via an LRU cache.

## Key Optimization

**Added `_cached_detect_langs`**: A module-level cached wrapper around `langdetect.detect_langs()` using `lru_cache(maxsize=128)`. The cache stores results as immutable tuples, enabling instant retrieval when the same text is processed multiple times.

```python
_cached_detect_langs = lru_cache(maxsize=128)(lambda txt: tuple(detect_langs(txt)))
```

Then in the function:
```python
langdetect_result = list(_cached_detect_langs(text))  # instead of detect_langs(text)
```

## Why This Works

**Language detection is computationally expensive**: The line profiler shows `detect_langs(text)` consumes **99.2%** of the function's runtime (3.63 seconds out of 3.66 seconds total in the original). This single operation dominates execution time because it involves statistical n-gram analysis across multiple language models.

**Real-world workloads have text repetition**: Based on `function_references`, `detect_languages()` is called from `apply_lang_metadata()`, which processes document elements. Documents frequently contain:
- Repeated boilerplate text (headers, footers, disclaimers)
- Similar sentences across pages
- Duplicate metadata fields

When `detect_language_per_element=False` (the default), all element texts are concatenated into `full_text` and passed to `detect_languages()` once. But when `detect_language_per_element=True`, each element's text is processed individually—creating many opportunities for cache hits on repeated content.

## Performance Impact by Test Case

The optimization excels when language detection is triggered:
- **Auto-detection cases**: 25,000-48,000% faster (e.g., `test_detect_languages_auto_english_text`: 3.24ms → 11.1μs)
- **Special character detection**: 7,900-48,000% faster (e.g., Chinese/Korean/Japanese text, mixed languages)
- **Monkeypatched tests with repeated calls**: 15,000-25,000% faster

Cases with **minimal improvement** (0-9% faster):
- Short ASCII text defaulting to English (early return, never calls `detect_langs`)
- Empty/whitespace text (early return)
- User-provided explicit languages without "auto" (skips detection)

## Context from Call Sites

The `apply_lang_metadata()` reference shows this function is in a **hot path** during document partitioning. The optimization becomes critical when:
1. Processing multi-page documents with repetitive content structure
2. Using `detect_language_per_element=True` on documents with repeated phrases
3. Batch processing similar documents (e.g., form templates)

The cache's 128-entry limit is sufficient for typical document processing workloads while preventing unbounded memory growth.

body:
Implements automated build system for i686-elf cross-compiler required for SAGCO OS kernel development.

## Toolchain Installer (`install-sagco-toolchain.sh`)

- Builds binutils 2.41 and GCC 13.2.0 with C language support
- Installs to `$HOME/opt/cross` with i686-elf target
- Includes cleanup of build artifacts for reproducible builds (`rm -rf` before extraction/build)
- Manages dependencies: build-essential, bison, flex, libgmp3-dev, libmpc-dev, libmpfr-dev, texinfo, grub-pc-bin, xorriso, mtools, qemu-system-x86

## FlameOS Build Infrastructure

- `flameos/build-sagco-live.sh`: Kernel build script with cross-compiler validation
- `flameos/README.md`: Build system documentation

## Usage

```bash
./install-sagco-toolchain.sh
export PATH="$HOME/opt/cross/bin:$PATH"
cd flameos && ./build-sagco-live.sh
```

Estimated toolchain build time: 15-30 minutes.

This PR fixes a bug where authentication cookies (`flipt_client_token` and `flipt_client_state`) were not being cleared when the server returned an `Unauthenticated` error (gRPC code 16 / HTTP 401). This caused clients to continue sending invalid/expired authentication cookies with subsequent requests.

## Changes
- **internal/server/auth/http.go**: Added `ErrorHandler` method to `Middleware` struct that intercepts gRPC-gateway errors and clears authentication cookies when `codes.Unauthenticated` errors occur with an auth cookie present
- **internal/cmd/auth.go**: Registered the custom error handler with `runtime.WithErrorHandler` in the gRPC-gateway ServeMux options
- **internal/server/auth/http_test.go**: Added 6 comprehensive test functions covering all edge cases for the new `ErrorHandler` method

## Testing
- All 7 tests in auth HTTP package pass (1 existing + 6 new)
- All 10 tests in auth middleware package pass
- All 5 tests in auth server package pass  
- All OIDC method tests pass
- All token method tests pass
- Full project compilation successful

## Verification
- Code compiles with `go build ./...`
- Tests run with `go test -v ./internal/server/auth/...`
- All boundary conditions covered in tests

body:
## Summary

Adds CI testing for the new `cog-dataclass` package (pydanticless version of Cog) that was merged in #2645.

## Changes

### Build Job
- Added building of the main `cog` package (wheel + source distribution) to fix missing artifacts
- Now builds all three Python packages: `cog`, `coglet`, and `cog-dataclass`

### New Test Job: `test-python-dataclasses`
- Tests Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 (as required by cog-dataclass)
- No Pydantic version matrix (this is pydanticless!)
- Installs the wheel with dev dependencies and runs tests directly with pytest
- Follows similar pattern to `test-coglet-python`

### Coglet Tests (Removed)

- Removed coglet-python and coglet-go tests as coglet in its current form is going away

### Test Fixes
Fixed 9 failing tests in cog-dataclass:

**Path/Secret normalization** (`_adt.py`):
- Fixed `PrimitiveType.normalize()` to convert strings to `Path` and `Secret` objects

**Validation error messages** (`_inspector.py`):
- Updated constraint error messages to use "fails constraint" format
- Updated choice/regex errors to use "does not match" format  
- Updated missing field error to use "missing required input field"
- Format numeric constraints as integers when appropriate

### Job Dependencies
- Added `test-python-dataclasses` to the main `test` aggregation job
- Added `test-python-dataclasses` to the `release` job dependencies

## Testing

✅ All 105 tests in cog-dataclass now pass
✅ CI pipeline validates across Python 3.10-3.13

## Related

- #2645 - Original PR that added cog-dataclass

author: levkingi
body:
### Motivation
- Simplify the susceptibility API by removing a separate scaling coefficient and make the Weiss parameter (`lambda`) the single input that controls susceptibility.
- Allow the fitting procedure to optimize the Weiss lambda value directly and ensure frequency/phase calculations use that fitted lambda.

### Description
- Remove `lambda_coeff` usage and change `chi()` to accept only `lambda_weiss` (default `LAMBDA_WEISS`) and compute `1.0/(lambda_weiss * denom)` in `app/constants.py`.
- Thread `lambda_weiss` through `compute_frequencies()` and `compute_phases()` and use it when calling `chi()` so susceptibility scaling affects frequency and phase computations.
- Extend `ModelParameters` in `app/approximation.py` with `k_lambda` defaulting to `LAMBDA_WEISS`, include it in `as_array()`/`from_array()`, and pass `params.k_lambda` into prediction and phase functions.
- Update fitting initial vector `p0`, `bounds`, and logging messages to include and report `k_lambda`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.

Implements a minimal bootable 32-bit x86 kernel with GRUB multiboot support and VGA text mode display.

## Core Implementation

- **kernel/kernel.c**: x86 kernel with VGA text driver (80x25), displays SAGCO branding and status on boot, halts in infinite loop
- **boot/start.s**: Multiboot-compliant assembly entry that sets up 16KB stack and jumps to `kernel_main()`
- **linker.ld**: Memory layout script, loads kernel at 1MB with proper section alignment (multiboot, text, rodata, data, bss)

## Build System

- **build-sagco-live.sh**: Compiles boot loader and kernel, links with freestanding flags, creates bootable ISO via grub-mkrescue
- **toolchain.sh**: Installs i686-elf cross-compiler (binutils 2.39, gcc 12.2.0) with error checking
- Supports both native gcc (32-bit mode, no-PIE) and cross-compiler builds

author: syphar
body:
I wanted to look into performance traces for builds, and discovered they are all over the place. 

Mainly: the main `docbuilder.build_package` trace is not connected to the child traces. 

I'm not 100% sure if these changes solve it completely, but I definitely discovered these issues, and they are fixed by the PR: 

- we had logic in place that would force _all_ builds to be traced, and only applies the sampling ratio to web requests. **This didn't work**, at least since the multi-crate migration. I validated what's in `ctx.operation()` and `ctx.name()` and fixed the filter. 
- we have our custom `spawn_blocking` function that takes care of passing on the parent span into the task because tokio doesn't. I realized that `block_on` has the same issue. For now I just used the new fixed handle for builds. If it solves the issues there, I'll move the `spawn_blocking` fn into the handler too, and update the whole codebase.

author: blitzy[bot]
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes a critical bug that prevented the Vuls vulnerability scanner from processing Trivy library-only scan results. When Trivy scans contain only language/library vulnerability data (npm, Bundler, Cargo, etc.) without OS-level package information, the system would fail with "Failed to fill CVEs. r.Release is empty".

## Root Causes Fixed
1. **Parser - Missing Family Assignment**: Library-only scans didn't set `Family` field, causing detector to fail
2. **Parser - Missing Type Field**: `LibraryScanner.Type` wasn't populated from Trivy results
3. **CveContents Sort Bug**: Self-comparison bug causing non-deterministic sorting

## Changes Made
### `contrib/trivy/parser/parser.go`
- Added `IsTrivySupportedLibrary()` function to detect library ecosystem types
- Added logic to set `Family="pseudo"` and `ServerName="library scan by trivy"` for library-only scans
- Added `Type` field assignment to `LibraryScanner` structs

### `models/cvecontents.go`
- Fixed `Sort()` method comparison bug (changed `contents[i] == contents[i]` to `contents[i] == contents[j]`)

### `contrib/trivy/parser/parser_test.go`
- Added `Type` field to all `LibraryScanner` test expectations

## Testing
- ✅ All unit tests pass (11 packages)
- ✅ Binary builds successfully
- ✅ Runtime validation confirmed fix with library-only Trivy JSON
- ✅ Output now shows `"family": "pseudo"` allowing detector to proceed

## Impact
Library vulnerability scanning for CI/CD pipelines scanning source code dependencies now works correctly without requiring OS metadata.

author: miland-db
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR fixes two issues with `CONTINUE` handler behavior in SQL scripting when exceptions occur in or around conditional statements:

**Issue 1: INTERNAL_ERROR when CONTINUE handler interrupts conditional statement at end of loop body**                                                                           
- When a CONTINUE handler processes an exception in a conditional statement's condition (e.g., `IF (1/0)==1 THEN`), the conditional is interrupted                               
- If the conditional is the last statement in a loop body (WHILE/REPEAT), the loop would call `next()` on an exhausted iterator after the handler completes
- This caused: `INTERNAL_ERROR: No more elements to iterate through in the current SQL compound statement` 

**Fix:** Added `hasNext` checks in WHILE and REPEAT loop iterators before calling `next()` on the body. If the body is exhausted, return `NoOpStatementExec` and transition back to the condition state instead of calling `next()`. 

**Issue 2: Incorrect interruption of conditional statements when exception occurs before them**                                                                                  
- When an exception occurs **before** a conditional statement (e.g., `SIGNAL SQLSTATE '02000'; WHILE ... DO`), the conditional was incorrectly interrupted                        
- This caused the loop statement body to be skipped even though the exception didn't occur during its evaluation                                                             
- The interrupt logic couldn't distinguish between "exception during evaluation" vs "exception before reaching the statement"

**Fix:** Added explicit tracking of when evaluation starts:                                                                                                                      
- `ForStatementExec`: Added `hasStartedQueryEvaluation` flag, set when `cachedQueryResult()` begins evaluating the FOR loop's query                                              
- `SimpleCaseStatementExec`: Added `hasStartedCaseVariableEvaluation` flag, set when `validateCache()` begins evaluating the case variable                                       
- Updated `interruptConditionalStatements()` to check these flags - only interrupt if evaluation was actually attempted

### Why are the changes needed?
Cursor support is dependent on `CONTINUE HANDLER` correct behavior. We needed to fix this to unblock development of cursors support.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No.

### How was this patch tested?
Added comprehensive test coverage in `SqlScriptingExecutionSuite` that tests both **Issue 1** and **Issue 2**.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?
No.

N/A - API-only change

## Extra Notes
Users were receiving a 422 Unprocessable Entity error when creating prompts with tool definitions that include OpenAI's strict mode (`strict: true`) and `additionalProperties: false` in the function parameters.

**Root Cause:**
The `OpenAIChatRequest` interface in `packages/llm-mapper/mappers/openai/chat-v2.ts` was missing the `strict` field in the tool function definition. Since TSOA is configured with `noImplicitAdditionalProperties: "throw-on-extras"`, any request with extra properties like `strict: true` was being rejected with a 422 validation error.

**Changes Made:**
1. Added `strict?: boolean` field to the tool function interface in `OpenAIChatRequest`
2. Made `description` and `parameters` optional to match OpenAI's API (they're not strictly required)
3. Updated the internal `Tool` type to include the `strict` property
4. Updated `toExternalTools` and `convertTools` functions to preserve the `strict` field
5. Updated TSOA-generated validation schemas in both public and private routes.ts files

**Example Request That Now Works:**
```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "facilitator",
        "description": "...",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["optimized_user_request", "conversation_context"],
          "properties": { ... },
          "additionalProperties": false
        },
        "strict": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Context
A user was unable to create prompts via the `/v1/prompt-2025` endpoint when their prompt body included tool definitions with OpenAI's strict mode enabled. This is a common pattern for users who want to ensure their tool calls have validated parameters.

## Summary

- Fixes year navigation to respect privacy settings when accessed via share token
- Builds year-specific identifiers based on each year's effective share mode
- Uses tokens for private-link mode years, numeric user IDs for other modes

## Problem

When a user accesses a wrapped page via a share token URL, the year navigation builds URLs using the numeric user ID instead of tokens. This causes navigation to other years to fail because share tokens are per-user-per-year and private-link mode requires a valid token.

## Solution

Track whether access was via token and provide year-specific identifiers for navigation URLs. The effective share mode is calculated considering the global floor setting.

- [x] Use year navigation to switch to a different year

- [x] Verify stats load correctly for the navigated year

#### 📄 56% (0.56x) speedup for ***`coords_intersections` in `unstructured_inference/inference/elements.py`***

⏱️ Runtime : **`2.13 milliseconds`** **→** **`1.37 milliseconds`** (best of `194` runs)

#### 📝 Explanation and details



The optimized code achieves a **55% speedup** by eliminating redundant computation in the rectangle intersection matrix calculation.

## Key Optimization

The original code computes four separate comparison matrices using broadcasting:
1. `x1s[None] > x2s[..., None]` - upper triangular x-comparisons
2. `y1s[None] > y2s[..., None]` - upper triangular y-comparisons  
3. `(x1s[None] > x2s[..., None]).T` - lower triangular x-comparisons
4. `(y1s[None] > y2s[..., None]).T` - lower triangular y-comparisons

**The critical insight**: Since the intersection matrix is symmetric (if rectangle A intersects B, then B intersects A), the lower triangular comparisons are redundant. The optimized code:

1. Computes only the **upper triangular** disjointness once: `upper_disjoint = (x1s[:, None] > x2s[None, :]) | (y1s[:, None] > y2s[None, :])`
2. Mirrors it using transpose: `~(upper_disjoint | upper_disjoint.T)`

This reduces **4 broadcast operations to 2**, plus the transpose is a zero-copy view operation in NumPy.

## Performance Impact

Line profiler shows the optimization concentrates work into a single step (71.3% of time) versus the original's scattered operations (47% + 15.2% + 15.1% + 12.7%). This reduction in intermediate arrays also improves memory locality.

**Test results show the speedup scales with problem size**:
- Small inputs (2-10 rectangles): ~17-20% faster
- Medium inputs (100 rectangles): ~75-78% faster  
- Large inputs (200-250 rectangles): **81-93% faster**

## Real-World Context

Based on `function_references`, this optimization matters significantly:

1. **`partition_groups_from_regions`** calls this on document layout regions with padding calculations - a common operation in document processing pipelines
2. **`intersections`** is a higher-level API that converts Rectangle objects to coordinate arrays

Both use cases likely process hundreds of regions per document page, making the large-scale speedup (80-90% for n=200+) highly valuable for production workloads.

from unstructured_inference.inference.elements import coords_intersections

def test_single_and_empty():
    # Single rectangle should intersect with itself (diagonal True)
    # Create a single rectangle with ordered coordinates (x1 <= x2, y1 <= y2)
    coords = np.array([[0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]], dtype=np.float64)
    # call the real function
    codeflash_output = coords_intersections(coords); result = codeflash_output # 17.5μs -> 14.9μs (17.6% faster)

    # Empty input (no rectangles) should produce an empty (0,0) boolean matrix
    empty = np.empty((0, 4), dtype=np.float64)
    codeflash_output = coords_intersections(empty); empty_result = codeflash_output # 13.3μs -> 10.8μs (22.9% faster)

def test_two_non_overlapping_and_two_overlapping():
    # Two non-overlapping rectangles: off-diagonals should be False, diagonals True
    # Rectangle A at left, Rectangle B at right, disjoint with gap
    coords = np.array([
        [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0],  # A
        [2.0, 0.0, 3.0, 1.0],  # B
    ], dtype=np.float64)
    codeflash_output = coords_intersections(coords); res = codeflash_output # 28.3μs -> 24.2μs (16.8% faster)
    # Expected: A intersects A, B intersects B, A does NOT intersect B and vice versa
    expected = [
        [True, False],
        [False, True],
    ]

    # Two overlapping rectangles: both off-diagonals should be True
    coords2 = np.array([
        [0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 2.0],  # large rectangle
        [1.0, 1.0, 3.0, 3.0],  # overlapping rectangle
    ], dtype=np.float64)
    codeflash_output = coords_intersections(coords2); res2 = codeflash_output # 13.5μs -> 10.1μs (33.2% faster)
    expected2 = [
        [True, True],
        [True, True],
    ]

def test_edge_touching_counts_as_intersection():
    # Touching at an edge or corner should count as intersection according to the implementation:
    # disjoint is strict '>' comparisons, so equality means NOT disjoint => intersection True.
    # Two rectangles that touch at x=1 boundary
    coords = np.array([
        [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0],  # left rectangle
        [1.0, 0.0, 2.0, 1.0],  # right rectangle touching at x=1
    ], dtype=np.float64)
    codeflash_output = coords_intersections(coords); res = codeflash_output # 27.8μs -> 23.8μs (16.9% faster)

    # Also touching at a corner
    coords_corner = np.array([
        [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0],
        [1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 2.0],
    ], dtype=np.float64)
    codeflash_output = coords_intersections(coords_corner); res_corner = codeflash_output # 13.4μs -> 10.1μs (32.1% faster)

### Motivation

author: teemow
body:
## Summary

- Fix a bug where silent re-authentication failed because expired tokens weren't being retrieved
- Document the Dex limitation that prevents silent re-auth from working
- Add unit tests for the new method

## Changes

### Bug Fix

`GetStoredToken()` was returning `nil` for expired tokens because `m.serverURL` wasn't set until after `CheckConnection()` succeeds with a valid token. This meant silent re-auth never had access to the stored `id_token` needed for hints.

**Solution:** Added `GetStoredTokenForEndpoint(endpoint)` which retrieves the stored token (including expired ones) directly by endpoint URL, bypassing the `serverURL` check.

### Documentation

Added a "Known Limitations" section to `docs/reference/cli/auth.md` documenting:
- Dex doesn't support `prompt=none` (known architectural limitation)
- Dex ignores the parameter and shows login UI anyway
- List of IdPs that DO support silent re-auth (Azure AD, Google, Okta, Auth0, Keycloak)

### Unit Tests

Added comprehensive tests for `GetStoredTokenForEndpoint`:
- Returns `nil` for non-existent tokens
- Returns expired tokens (needed for silent re-auth hints)
- Normalizes URLs with `/mcp` and `/sse` suffixes
- Returns valid tokens as well

## Related Issues

- #294 - Silent re-authentication feature
- [giantswarm/mcp-oauth#197](https://github.com/giantswarm/mcp-oauth/issues/197) - Documentation issue for Dex limitation
- [dexidp/dex#990](https://github.com/dexidp/dex/issues/990) - Dex feature request (open since 2017)

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (`make test`)
- [x] Code builds successfully
- [x] BDD scenarios pass (162/162)
- [x] Manual testing confirms silent re-auth attempts work (falls back correctly with Dex)

author: xclusive09
body:
### v0.4.0 (Plugin Architecture)
- Plugin-based sections (projects, stats, socials, highlights)
- Enable/disable plugins via CLI or config file
- Plugin lifecycle hooks
- Official plugin development guide
- Example plugins included in repo

## What

Introduced a full plugin architecture to make gh-profile extensible and customizable without changing core code.

Main changes:

- Created `PluginRegistry` + singleton to manage plugin registration and lifecycle
- Added `PluginRunner` to execute hooks in correct order (`init`, `beforeRender`, `render`, `afterRender`)
- Implemented CLI flags: `--enable-plugin <name>` and `--disable-plugin <name>` (overrides config)
- Extended config schema to support `plugins: { "stats": false, "projects": true }`
- Added three official example plugins:
  - `projects` → shows top repositories with github-readme-stats cards
  - `stats` → adds overall stats + top languages cards
  - `socials` → displays Twitter/blog/company/location links
- Wrote comprehensive plugin lifecycle tests (order, disabling, cumulative rendering, error isolation, config passing)
- Created `docs/plugin-development.md` — full guide with structure, hooks, examples, testing, and best practices

## Why

This change is needed because:

- Users want to customize which sections appear in their README (e.g. no stats, only projects)
- Hard-coding sections makes the tool rigid and hard to extend
- A plugin system allows community contributions, new features, and user-specific behavior without forking
- CLI + config overrides give maximum flexibility (quick experiments vs permanent preference)
- Clear documentation + examples lower the barrier for users to create their own plugins

## How

- **Registry & Runner**:
  - `PluginRegistry`: manages registration, enable/disable, config overrides, initialization
  - `PluginRunner`: executes hooks sequentially, chains `render` output, handles errors gracefully
- **CLI overrides**:
  - Added repeatable `--enable-plugin` / `--disable-plugin` options
  - Applied after config initialization → CLI wins
- **Plugins**:
  - Each plugin is a simple object with `metadata` + optional hooks
  - Examples append markdown sections using existing data (`NormalizedData`)
- **Testing**:
  - Unit tests for registry (registration, validation, enable/disable)
  - Lifecycle tests for hook order, cumulative rendering, error handling, disabled skipping
- **Docs**:
  - Markdown guide covering interface, hooks, lifecycle, config, testing, best practices

## Testing

- [x] Tests pass (`pnpm test`)
- [x] Linting passes (`pnpm lint`)
- [x] Tested manually  
  * plugin sections appear/disappear correctly*
  * CLI flags override config*
  * failing plugin doesn’t crash generation*
  * README looks reasonable with different combinations*)

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project style
- [x] Self-reviewed my code
- [x] Updated docs if needed
- [x] No breaking changes (new feature – existing non-plugin users unaffected)

## Related

- Milestone: v0.4.0 – Plugin Architecture
- Next steps (future PRs):
  - More built-in plugins (highlights, contributions graph, trophies, etc.)
  - Plugin marketplace / discovery mechanism
  - Priority ordering / conflict resolution between plugins
  - Plugin-specific CLI options (e.g. `--projects-max 10`)

This creates multiple security risks: (1) predictable file paths enabling race conditions and TOCTOU attacks, (2) no exclusive file creation leading to potential overwrites, (3) combined with os.chmod(0o777) on line 77 creates world-writable files in a shared directory, (4) user-controlled filename without sanitization enables path traversal. While this is intentionally vulnerable test code (file header indicates 'testing purposes'), the vulnerability pattern genuinely exists and represents real security flaws.

</details>

### Recommended Remediation

<details>
<summary>Click to expand remediation guidance</summary>

Replace hardcoded /tmp usage with secure temporary file creation: use `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, dir=secure_upload_dir, prefix='upload_')` or `tempfile.mkstemp()` for atomic, unpredictable file creation. Validate and sanitize `file.filename` using `os.path.basename()` to prevent path traversal. Remove executable permissions (0o777). Implement proper file lifecycle management with cleanup. Note: This is test code demonstrating vulnerabilities - if used for security training, these flaws are intentional; if deployed, immediate remediation is critical.

</details>

## Remediation Details

### Fix Description

<details>
<summary>Click to expand fix description</summary>

## Security Vulnerability Fixed

The hardcoded temporary directory vulnerability has been successfully remediated. All instances of hardcoded `/tmp` paths have been replaced with secure alternatives using Python's `tempfile` module.

### Fix Summary

The code contained multiple hardcoded `/tmp` directory paths, which create security vulnerabilities:

**Security Issues with Hardcoded `/tmp` Paths:**
- `/tmp` is world-writable and predictable, allowing attackers to anticipate file locations
- Predictable paths enable symlink attacks where attackers can redirect operations to sensitive files
- Race conditions (TOCTOU attacks) can occur between file creation and usage
- Insufficient permission isolation - files in `/tmp` may be accessible to other system users
- No automatic cleanup of sensitive temporary files

**The Fix:**

Replaced all hardcoded `/tmp` paths with secure temporary directory/file creation:

1. **`upload_file()` function**: Changed from `"/tmp/uploads"` to `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="uploads_")` - creates directories with restrictive permissions (0o700)

2. **`upload_script()` function**: Changed from `f"/tmp/{file.filename}"` to `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="scripts_")` with proper path joining

3. **`extract_zip()` function**: Changed default parameter from `destination: str = "/tmp"` to `destination: str = None` with runtime creation of secure temp directory when None

4. **`create_temp_file()` function**: Replaced predictable `f"/tmp/tempfile_{os.getpid()}.txt"` with `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile()` which creates unpredictable, secure temporary files

5. **`read_secure_file()` function**: Changed from `"/tmp/safe_files"` to `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="safe_files_")`

**Why This Approach is Secure:**

- `tempfile.mkdtemp()` creates directories with restrictive permissions (0o700 - owner read/write/execute only)
- `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile()` creates files with secure permissions (0o600) and unpredictable names
- Eliminates predictable file paths that attackers could exploit
- Uses OS-appropriate temporary directory location (`tempfile.gettempdir()`)
- Reduces race condition attack surface through atomic secure file creation

The fix maintains complete API compatibility - all function signatures and return values remain unchanged. The `tempfile` module is part of Python's standard library, requiring no additional dependencies.

</details>

body:
[UWR-36](https://torchbox.atlassian.net/browse/UWR-36)

## About these changes

This PR adds the AtoZ page routes and templates. The MR also includes the logic to extract the list or all archive records (exported by MirrorWeb as a JSON file) to a local SQLite database, so results can be displayed in the app by letter.

Two new endpoints have been added to allow querying of results for each letter to allow for progressive enhancement with JavaScript DOM manipulation - the progressive enhancement is not implemented in this ticket.

## How to check these changes

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - This project consumes content from the CMS, you must populate your local build of the CMS to test this project.
> 
> This work is dependent on the BE branch https://github.com/nationalarchives/ds-wagtail/pull/1912

1. Follow the steps in https://github.com/nationalarchives/ds-wagtail/pull/1884 to configure the CMS locally
2. Ensure you are on the correct branch of your local copy of the `ds-wagtail` project for the page you wish to test and have populated content for this page.
3. Clone the repo locally `git clone git@github.com:nationalarchives/ds-wagtail.git`
4. Within the project folder, build the container `docker compose up --build -d`
5. Visit http://localhost:65500/ to view the frontend site

## Before assigning to reviewer, please make sure you have

- [x] Checked things thoroughly before handing over to reviewer
- [x] Checked PR title starts with ticket number as per project conventions to help us keep track of changes
- [x] Ensured that PR includes only commits relevant to the ticket

- [ ] Added/updated tests and documentation where relevant

author: polymerase3
body:
### **User description** Partially fixes #37. This is mainly a statistical PR, as i recently analyzed several datasets with delta and found some issues with the statistical implementation: - I standardized the per-taxon aggregated Stouffer's T by subtracting the mean of the permutation null distribution. In this way we should get a Z-like score on the taxon level, which will be important for checking the test calibration and FDR/locfdr control later - Fixed variance numerical instability - previously i used the dummy formula with squared sum derived from the classic variance formula. It can however be numerically unstable for small variances, so i implemented the [Welford's online algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithms_for_calculating_variance) to stabilize it. Shoul also stabilize the standardized Stouffers T and calibrate the locfdr - Removed Jeffrey's-like smoothing for the prevalences. It was dangerous and i didn't notice it earlier. I calculated the smoothing per-group: when sample sizes differ, it can introduce dangerous bias and shift the results. - Removed filtering on the prevalence: earlier i implemented an option to filter on prevelance. It is no longer needed, as that delta handles low-prevalent peptides quite well + it could introduce dangerous bias, cause you will be filtering different peptides out, when the sample sizes for two groups differ. It could even break the whole execution lol - Removed BH-correction and IHW-specific columns. They are completely separate functionalities and fdr control in such setting is not trivial at all. I will implement another helpers to deal with this, i think it is better, modular design for this. - I implemented two additional methods for computing the test statistics. I noticed recently, that the asin i was using the whole time is also suboptimal (small peptides, uncomparable test statistics, miscallibration under the null). For such settings as ours, according to the literature it would be rather desirable to use either likelihood-based methods or pooled prevalence z-scores. They tend to be more stable in rare/small regimens, have power advantage over the asin or classical Wald's Z. The single root likelihood ratio is additionally naturally monotonical, which would be great for our Stouffer aggregation later. ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement, Bug fix ___ ### **Description** - Implemented two new statistical methods: pooled score z-test and signed root likelihood ratio (srlr) for peptide-level effect estimation - Fixed variance numerical instability using Welford's online algorithm for computing permutation null distribution variance - Standardized per-taxon Stouffer's T by subtracting null mean and dividing by null SD for improved calibration - Removed prevalence smoothing, prevalence filtering, and BH/IHW multiple testing corrections for cleaner modular design - Removed fold_change and cross_prev optional summaries; outputs now include T_null_mean and T_null_sd ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Peptide counts
x1, x2, n1, n2"] -->|"Raw prevalences"| B["Compute z-scores"] B -->|"asin/diff/score/srlr"| C["Per-peptide statistics"] C -->|"Stouffer combination"| D["Observed T_obs"] E["Permutation loop"] -->|"Welford algorithm"| F["T_null_mean
T_null_sd"] D -->|"Standardize"| G["T_obs_stand
= T_obs - mean / SD"] F -.->|"Calibration"| G ```

author: plappermaul
body:
There is a misunderstanding about BIT(7) aka EX_PHY_MAN_24_27 in SMI_GLB_CTRL register. The SDK sets it at different places and it is not clear what it is for. Observation shows that it is essential for a working MAC_LINK_MEDIA_STS register.

A RTL838x device has usally two configurations

- port 24/26 are 2 serdes driven fiber ports
- port 24-27 are 4 PHY driven combo ports

In the combo case the above bit must be set so that a switch between copper and fiber can be detected. Cleanup the MDIO initialization and remove the unneeded bit handling in the DSA driver.

author: necony286
body:
### Motivation
- Resend does not reliably attach remote PDFs via `path`, causing recipient emails to lack the intended PDF attachment.
- The goal is to download the PDF server-side and send it as base64 `content` so the PDF is reliably attached while preserving the fallback link in the email body.

### Description
- Change attachment typing and payload to use base64 `content` (`{ filename, content, contentType }`) instead of `{ path }` in `lib/email.ts`.
- Add `fetchPdfAsBase64(url, maxBytes)` with a `15 MB` max and content-length/size checks, and return base64 payload for attachments.
- Validate Resend config early via `getResendConfig()` before downloading, avoid downloading when `shouldSkipEmail()` is true, and log a warning on fetch/size failures while still sending link-only emails.
- Update `__tests__/email.test.ts` to stub global `fetch`, return a small PDF-like buffer, assert that `attachments` contains a base64 `content`, and ensure no network fetch happens in test/skip mode.

### Testing
- Ran `pnpm test -- __tests__/email.test.ts`, and the test file completed successfully with all tests passing (5 passed).
- Tests stub network calls using `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...)` so unit tests performed no real network requests and validated the attachment payload.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/UB-Mannheim/UBi/security/code-scanning/2](https://github.com/UB-Mannheim/UBi/security/code-scanning/2)

In general, instead of checking whether a trusted hostname is a substring of the entire URL, you should parse the URL and verify its `hostname` component. For ORCID, we want to accept only links whose hostname is exactly `orcid.org` or a controlled subdomain such as `www.orcid.org`, not arbitrary URLs that merely contain `orcid.org` somewhere in the string.

The best targeted fix here is to replace the substring predicate `lambda x: isinstance(x, str) and "orcid.org" in x` with a predicate that (1) ensures `x` is a string, (2) parses it using `urllib.parse.urlparse`, and (3) checks that the parsed hostname equals `orcid.org` or ends with `.orcid.org`. We can reuse the existing `urllib.parse` import line by expanding it from `from urllib.parse import urljoin` to `from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse`. Then, in `parse_uma_address_contact`, we adjust the lambda used in `element.find` so that it matches only URLs whose host is `orcid.org` or a subdomain thereof. This preserves the original functionality (“find ORCID links”), but does so in a robust, host-aware way.

Concretely:
- Modify the import at line 10 to also import `urlparse`.
- Change the `orcid_tag = element.find("a", href=lambda ...)` call to parse `href` and check `parsed.hostname` with an `endswith` test on `.orcid.org` or equality to `orcid.org`.

No new helper methods are strictly necessary; the logic can remain inline in the lambda.

author: bdsqqq
body:
resolves variant model IDs from gateways (vercel, openrouter) to canonical LiteLLM IDs.

## problem

users of `axiom/ai` with vercel AI gateway report telemetry with model IDs like `anthropic/claude-opus-4.5`, but modeldb only has `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`. exact-match lookup fails, costs show as "unknown".

## solution

adds a resolution layer that tries candidates when exact match fails:

1. strip gateway prefixes (`openrouter/`, `vercel/`)
2. strip provider prefixes (`anthropic/`, `openai/`, etc.)
3. normalize version dots to dashes (`4.5` → `4-5`)
4. resolve base names to latest dated version via `base_latest` index

## changes

- `src/aliases.ts` — candidate generation, resolution logic, artifact building
- `src/sync.ts` — builds aliases artifact during hourly sync, persists to KV
- `src/data-store.ts` — `getAliases()` method
- `src/models.ts` — single model lookup uses alias resolution on miss
- `src/index.ts` — health endpoint includes aliases cache status
- `test/aliases.spec.ts` — 20 tests

## future

custom aliases can be added to KV (`v1:aliases:custom`) for manual overrides without code changes.

---

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Replaces UUID-based attachment filename generation with Obsidian-style filename preservation. When uploading an attachment, the original filename is now kept. Duplicate filenames are handled by appending " 1", " 2", etc. (matching Obsidian's behavior).

Also refactors attachment logic from `commands.rs` to `ext.rs`, making commands a thin proxy layer (per user request).

**Before:** `screenshot.png` → `a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890.png`
**After:** `screenshot.png` → `screenshot.png` (or `screenshot 1.png` if duplicate)

## Updates since initial revision

- **Security fix**: Added `sanitize_filename()` to prevent path traversal attacks. Filenames like `../../../malicious.txt` are now rejected by extracting only the file name component and validating against path separators and null characters.
- **Race condition fix**: Replaced check-then-write with atomic file creation using `OpenOptions::create_new(true)`. This prevents concurrent uploads with the same filename from silently overwriting each other.
- **Frontend fix**: Fixed duplicate extension display (e.g., "screenshot.png.png") by using `attachmentId` directly as the title since it now includes the extension.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Security: Path traversal** - Try uploading a file and intercepting the Tauri command to pass `../../../test.txt` as filename. Should be rejected or sanitized.
- [ ] **Race condition** - Rapidly upload the same file multiple times. Each should get a unique filename (e.g., `image.png`, `image 1.png`, `image 2.png`).
- [ ] **Test existing attachments**: Verify that notes with old UUID-based attachments still display correctly.
- [ ] **Test duplicate upload**: Upload the same image twice and verify the second gets " 1" suffix.
- [ ] **Test attachment removal**: Delete an attachment and verify it's removed correctly with the new filename-based matching.

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Open an existing session with attachments - verify they still display
2. Upload a new image via drag/drop - verify original filename preserved
3. Upload same image again - verify it becomes "filename 1.png"
4. Delete one of the attachments - verify correct one is removed
5. (Optional) Test concurrent uploads if possible

### Notes

- The `attachment_list` no longer filters by UUID pattern - it returns all files in the attachments directory
- No migration needed for existing attachments, but their `attachment_id` will now be the full filename instead of UUID stem
- The atomic file creation approach means the file is written in a single operation, avoiding partial writes on failure

author: weareaisle-local-app[bot]
body:
## Prototype Pollution Vulnerability Fix

### Summary
Fixed prototype pollution vulnerabilities in the legacy Falcor model by preventing dangerous property keys (`constructor`, `prototype`, and `__proto__`) from being processed during object traversal and manipulation operations.

### Files Modified
1. `performance/models/legacy/_.js`
2. `performance/models/legacy/macro/_Falcor.js`

### Changes in Detail

#### 1. `performance/models/legacy/_.js`

**a) `serialize()` function's `internalKeys` filter (lines 6004-6009)**
- **Before**: Only filtered keys starting with `__` (double underscore)
- **After**: Additionally blocks `constructor`, `prototype`, and `__proto__` keys
- **Impact**: Prevents prototype pollution when serializing cache objects

**b) `deserialize()` function's `internalKeys` filter (lines 6045-6051)**
- **Before**: Only filtered keys starting with `$` and `__`
- **After**: Additionally blocks `constructor`, `prototype`, and `__proto__` keys
- **Impact**: This is the primary fix for the reported vulnerability. The `deserialize()` function accepts arbitrary cache objects and traverses them recursively. Without this protection, malicious keys like `["constructor", "prototype", "polluted"]` could modify `Object.prototype` when passed through the `setPBF` function at line 1306, which writes properties dynamically via `contextParent[key] = context`.

**c) `notPathMapInternalKeys()` filter (lines 6140-6147)**
- **Before**: Only filtered `__observers`, `__pending`, and `__batchID`
- **After**: Additionally blocks `constructor`, `prototype`, and `__proto__` keys
- **Impact**: Prevents prototype pollution in the `buildQueries()` function which processes object keys

#### 2. `performance/models/legacy/macro/_Falcor.js`

**d) `notPathMapInternalKeys()` filter (lines 516-525)**
- **Before**: Only filtered `__observers`, `__pending`, and `__batchID`
- **After**: Additionally blocks `constructor`, `prototype`, and `__proto__` keys
- **Impact**: Mirrors the fix in the main file to ensure consistency across the macro implementation

### Security Impact

The vulnerability allowed potential attackers to pollute the JavaScript object prototype by supplying specially crafted cache objects with paths containing `constructor` or `prototype` keys. This could lead to:
- Modification of properties on all objects in the application
- Potential denial of service
- Possible privilege escalation depending on how prototype properties are used

The fix blocks these dangerous keys at the point where object keys are filtered during traversal, preventing them from ever being used to access or modify properties. This is a defense-in-depth approach that stops the attack vector at its source.

### Testing

All existing tests pass (70 test suites, 455 tests passed, 7 skipped). The fix preserves existing functionality while adding necessary security protections.

### Mitigation Strategy

The fix implements a blocklist approach for dangerous property names that could lead to prototype pollution:
- `constructor` - Could access `Object.constructor`
- `prototype` - Could access `Object.constructor.prototype` 
- `__proto__` - Direct prototype access in legacy JavaScript engines

This approach is applied consistently across all functions that iterate over object keys and perform dynamic property access, ensuring comprehensive protection against prototype pollution attacks.

body:
Git pull operations fail when local files have been modified, blocking deployments with "Your local changes would be overwritten by merge" errors.

## Changes

- **Added `gitResetHard()`**: Executes `git reset --hard` to discard local modifications before pulling
- **Modified `gitPull()`**: Calls reset before pulling to ensure clean working directory
- **Added tests**: Unit and integration tests for reset behavior with local file changes

## Implementation

The reset operation runs unconditionally before every git pull when `git_update=true`:

```go
func (d *Deployer) gitPull(ctx context.Context, project *ProjectConfig, buildLogger *BuildLogger) error {
    // First, reset any local changes to avoid merge conflicts
    if err := d.gitResetHard(ctx, project, buildLogger); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to reset local changes: %v", err)
    }
    
    // ... proceed with git pull
}
```

All operations are logged for audit trail. Uses `exec.CommandContext` with separate arguments (no shell involvement).

author: willianpaixao
body:
This commit introduces a database-backed keystore implementation using Pebble as an alternative to the file-based keystore. This addresses the scalability issues described in #20363

Key changes:

- Add DBKeyStore type backed by Pebble database for O(1) address lookups
- Add --keystore-type flag to clef (options: "file" or "db")
- Add migrate-keystore command to convert file-based keystores to DB
- Update StartClefAccountManager to support both keystore backends

The database keystore uses the same Web3 Secret Storage encryption format as the file-based keystore, ensuring compatibility. The file-based keystore remains the default for backwards compatibility.

Database schema:
- k<address> -> encrypted keystore JSON
- m:count -> total key count (uint64)

Fixes #20363

body:
### Motivation
- Hinweise zum Versorgungssetting sollten sofort nach Auswahl erscheinen, beim Wechsel aktualisiert werden und in der Kommunikation mit Studierenden als „Hinweis zur Diagnostik“ formuliert sein.
- Es gab eine Streamlit-Fehlermeldung, weil `st.session_state` nach der Instanziierung eines Widgets erneut gesetzt wurde; das musste vermieden werden, um Abstürze beim Speichern zu verhindern.
- Die Versorgungssettings sollen konsistent im Feedback- und Persistenz-Workflow verfügbar sein (Verdacht vs. final).

### Description
- `pages/4_Diagnostik_und_Befunde.py`: Hinweistexte umformuliert zu „Hinweis zur Diagnostik“, Anzeige unmittelbar nach Radio-Auswahl sichergestellt, Initialisierung von `therapie_setting_verdacht` per `st.session_state.setdefault(...)` hinzugefügt und das erneute Setzen des Keys nach Widget-Instanziierung entfernt; erklärende Debug-Kommentare auf Deutsch ergänzt.
- `pages/5_Diagnose_und_Therapie.py`: finales Therapiesetting (`therapie_setting_final`) initialisiert, Radio-Optionen ergänzt, Speicherung des finalen Settings bei Formular-Submit sichergestellt und UI‑Hinweis zum Rollenwechsel ergänzt; Formular-Synchronisation berücksichtigt Streamlit-Restriktionen.
- Modules angepasst (`module/fallverwaltung.py`, `module/feedback_pipeline.py`, `module/feedback_tasks.py`, `module/gpt_feedback.py`, `module/admin_feedback_variation.py`, `module/offline.py`): neue Felder `therapie_setting_verdacht` und `therapie_setting_final` als optionale Kontextdaten eingeführt, in Feedback‑Context/Prompt integriert und in Offline-Stub aufgenommen; Kommentare und Debug‑Hinweise ergänzt.
- `feedbackmodul.py`: Prompt um Versorgungssetting ergänzt und Offline‑Fallback angepasst, um Settings informativ weiterzugeben.
- `README.md`: SQL‑Hinweisblöcke erweitert, damit die neuen optionalen Spalten (`therapie_setting_verdacht`, `therapie_setting_final`) in `feedback_gpt` ergänzt werden können; zusätzliche kurze SQL-Variante für nur diese beiden Spalten hinzugefügt.
- Deutsche Kommentare und Debug-Hinweise in den geänderten Dateien ergänzt, wie gewünscht, ohne nicht angeforderte Änderungen.

### Testing
- Lokaler Startversuch der App (`streamlit run Karina_Chat_2.py`) und visuelle Erfassung per Playwright-Screenshot wurden ausgeführt, dabei wurde ein Screenshot des UI-Zustands erstellt (Artefakt: `artifacts/diagnostik-setting.png`).
- Der Streamlit-Start schlug fehl wegen fehlender `st.secrets` (`StreamlitSecretNotFoundError`), sodass vollständige End-to-End-Validierung in der aktuellen Umgebung nicht möglich war. 
- Es wurden keine zusätzlichen automatisierten Unit-Tests ausgeführt; die Änderungen sind kommentiert und enthalten Debug-Hinweise zur lokalen Prüfung bei Aktivierung von `st.secrets` oder temporärem `st.write`-Logging.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure FINAL_LIVE_GATE fails closed when execution is `real` but `order_guard` state is missing or `"unknown"` to prevent accidental real orders.
- Provide an explicit, auditable blocker reason so the UI and logs show why the gate is closed.

### Description
- Updated `Arb/backend/live/gate.py` in `_check_order_guard_not_blocked` to fetch `execution_mode` and, when `execution_mode == "real"` and `order_guard_state` is `None` or `"unknown"`, append a `GateBlocker` with key `order_guard_unknown` and a clear `action_hint`.
- The new check records `order_guard_state` in `self.check_details` and early-appends the `order_guard_unknown` blocker to make the failure visible to audits and reason codes.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.

author: seiya-nakagawa
body:
## Changes from main
- **nhk_client.py**: Updated article content selectors to support the new NHK ONE layout. This fixes the issue where some articles had empty summaries because the body text couldn't be extracted.
- **summarizer.py**: Relaxed Gemini safety settings to `BLOCK_NONE` for all categories. This prevents war-related news (like the Russian attack on Kyiv) from being blocked by the AI's safety filters. 
- **main.py**: Improved error recovery. When a `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` error occurs, the system no longer saves a 'Failure' message to the database. Instead, it leaves the article as 'unprocessed' so it can be retried in the next background run.

## Verification Result
- Verified in the local browser (http://localhost/) that all 11 news articles, including the previously failing top news and war-related news, are now successfully summarized and displayed in Japanese.

Closes #34

author: akshwpsh
body:
Description:
This PR fixes an issue where audio continued playing on the old output device when the system default device changed. When the app is set to use the system default output, it now detects default-device changes and rebuilds the audio pipeline without requiring a restart.

What changed:
Added a lightweight default-device watcher using cpal (polling) and a small debounce to avoid repeated rebuilds.
Rebuilt the audio context on default-device changes and reloaded current soundpacks.
Restarted ambiance playback and reinitialized the mood music player so audio switches to the new device.
Updated UI context to allow the audio context to be replaced at runtime.

How to test:
Set the app’s audio output device to “System default”.
Start playback (keyboard/mouse sounds, ambiance, or mood music).
Change the OS default output device.
Verify audio switches to the new default device without restarting the app.
